outcomes: In a Go repository, each Go module is a component, named by its directory and its module path, found from go.work and go.mod
Each changed file maps to the module that holds it, and each module lists the repository modules it requires or replaces, so the change analysis can list the dependent modules
A Go test or coverage report that names a package or a file by its import path maps to the repository file and the module that holds it
Each module's go.mod gives the dependency versions it locks, so the change analysis can diff them between the base and the commit
nonGoals: Running go, reading the module cache or the network: the detector reads files only
Computing the changed and dependent components, the tests and coverage per component, the changed-line coverage and the dependency changes: the change analyses own them
Reading the content of test and coverage reports: the evidence readers own it
Running as its own extension over the workspace probe transport, which needs the host call of Putnami/putnami#742

requirements.text: Each directory a root go.work uses is a component of source workspace; each other go.mod the bounded walk finds, skipping .git, node_modules, vendor, testdata and directories whose name starts with a dot or an underscore, is a component of source manifest. A component's id is its directory relative to the repository root, . for the root, its name is the module path and its ecosystem is go. A file belongs to the innermost component whose directory holds it. A go.work or go.mod that cannot be read or parsed is a diagnostic. A go.mod only the lenient grammar reads keeps its module path and requires without its replace directives; one no grammar reads still makes its directory a component, without a name or edges.

A component depends on each other component whose module path its go.mod requires, after the replace directives of its go.mod and of the root go.work, and on each component a local replace directive of its go.mod points to. A local replace resolves against the directory of the file that holds it. A require of a module the repository does not hold is no edge, and a component never depends on itself.

An import path, as a go test -json event, a gotestsum or go-junit-report suite name and a go test -coverprofile file name write it, maps to the path below the component whose module path is its longest prefix on a slash boundary, and to that component. An import path no component's module path prefixes maps to nothing.

The locked dependencies of a go.mod are its requires, each with the version the go.mod's replace directives select and whether it is indirect. A require replaced by a local directory, or of a module the repository holds, is not a locked dependency. Each component names its go.mod as its lockfile and its go.mod and go.sum as watched files. Versions compare by Go's semantic version order.

The detection is also a workspace probe answer of @putnami/observe: one project per component, its module path and go.mod as source name and source file, its dependencies as component paths attributed to go-module, its go.mod and go.sum as watched files, the root go.work as a watched file. The answer validates against the workspace protocol's probe rules.
